reuse.why: The tolerance is still computed inline as Math.round(Math.abs(x)*0.075) in both copies, even though shared/rules.ts already exports getApproxNumberThreshold, and no shared worst-case function is introduced.

duplication.why: The worst-case rule is kept as two hand-maintained copies (scheduleModel.toExternal and computeSchedulePreviewTransactions), and the diff patches both with the same edit.

placement.why: Each edit is made where the copy already lives, but the rule belongs in shared/schedules.ts as one function that the API model calls.

scope.why: Only the two rule copies and their tests change.

maintainability.why: Any future change to the rule has to find and update both copies again, and the two copies already disagree in small ways (null handling, >= versus >).

bypasses_abstraction.where: Both copies compute the approximate tolerance inline instead of calling shared/rules.ts getApproxNumberThreshold

disguised_duplication.where: The same worst-case expression lives in api-models.ts scheduleModel.toExternal and shared/schedules.ts computeSchedulePreviewTransactions, written with different null checks and nesting
